races.name: Tom Halliday Memorial Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bannister
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type who has shown good form at 2m-2m2f on Good going (sim-going 14/15, one win, five places), but returning after 234 days off is a significant concern; if fit, he stays well and could emerge from a midfield group if the race sets up for late runners.
runners_data.comment: Absent for 234 days and winless in his last five, Bannister returns in a first-time tongue-tie. He can be consistent and handles this ground, but found this course and trip beyond him last time out — today's 20 furlongs poses the same question.

runners_data.name: Oneinthewell
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up performer whose recent form has come entirely on soft ground (five runs on Soft/Heavy), making this Good surface his first proper test on a quicker surface; trainer James Owen in fair recent form (7/37) but the going switch is the defining question for this runner.
runners_data.comment: Back from 146 days off and stepping down from his latest outing at Catterick, Oneinthewell has form over this distance and sets up as a real threat rated 2nd on our figures. First-time cheekpieces, though all his best form has come on softer surfaces than today.

runners_data.name: Lakefield Flyer
runners_data.note: Ran just five days ago — the shortest prep in the field — and that freshness could be a positive or a negative; a genuine hold-up horse at heart whose best form on Good (2W7P sim-going) is strong, though racing in a compressed midfield rather than from the rear means a STYLE_FIT discount of 0.92 is warranted and a clean run through is not guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Stratford last time off a mark 9lb higher than today's, Lakefield Flyer arrives at the top of our ratings having shown he acts over this distance and going. First-time tongue-tie, and the lighter weight makes him even more attractive; inconsistency is his one caveat.

runners_data.name: William Of York
runners_data.note: Sole prominent-style runner in the field aside from the leader, giving him the clearest tactical position to track Gone In Sixty; however, his record in this trip range on Good is thin (0W1P) and a run of pulling-up and unseating efforts in recent starts (UP-06P) makes reliability the key concern.
runners_data.comment: Dropped to a much reduced mark after a run of failures including two pull-ups in recent starts, William Of York returns in first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces. He likes to bowl along from the front and acts over this trip; a badly out-of-form trainer is the concern.

runners_data.name: Captain Connor
runners_data.note: Four-year-old lightly campaigned on soft ground, stepping onto Good for the first time; a natural hold-up horse compressed into midfield by the field shape (STYLE_FIT 0.90), and with no sim-going data on this surface and limited experience over this trip, he faces the most question marks of any runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Absent for 127 days and making his handicap debut, Captain Connor was pulled up at Kelso last time and has plenty to find, ranked 7th. First-time cheekpieces; the longer trip should suit, but he needs significant improvement to feature.

runners_data.name: Gone In Sixty
runners_data.note: The race's only front-runner and therefore the one horse guaranteed to get his preferred position; his 13/15 sim-going record on Good is compelling and recent form of 26-4F2 shows he regularly hits the frame when completing, making him the natural pace controller and a serious player if he holds on.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just over a length at Southwell last time off a slightly lower mark, Gone In Sixty arrives in fair shape over a trip he handles on suitable going. A course configuration like this should suit his preferences, and rated 4th on our figures he must be respected.

runners_data.name: Makinbecon
runners_data.note: Won at 18f on Good just 12 days ago, giving him a fitness edge and course-relevant form; however, his natural hold-up style means he will not get the rear ground he prefers and will be pressed into a midfield role (STYLE_FIT 0.92) — his best hope is the recent win having sharpened him for a forward move from the middle of the pack.
runners_data.comment: Third at the same mark as today on his latest outing, Makinbecon also got his head in front at Newton Abbot on his penultimate start and may have more to offer on his point form. Effective over this distance on this ground; first-time tongue-tie, and still on a fair mark.

runners_data.name: Time Was
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has been placed repeatedly at 20f on Soft but has a very limited record on Good (0W1P sim-going); placed into midfield due to field compression (STYLE_FIT 0.92), and with a conditional jockey claim from Oscar Palmer(3) as the main positive angle, he needs a strong pace to materialise — which this race is unlikely to produce.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a handicap hurdle here last time when asked to tackle this trip, Time Was is ranked last on our figures and has been inconsistent throughout. First-time cheekpieces, and effective at today's distance; but her recent form makes her hard to recommend.

races.paceDynamic: Gone In Sixty is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 2m4½f conditional jockeys' handicap hurdle and, with no obvious challenger for the lead, he will set a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front under Rian Corcoran. The remainder of the field — Bannister, Oneinthewell, Lakefield Flyer, Captain Connor, Makinbecon and Time Was — are all natural hold-up or rear-tracking types, meaning the pace will be sustainable and the tempo dictated entirely by Gone In Sixty's comfort level. William Of York is the only horse with any genuine prominent profile to push forward in behind, but even he has a patchy recent record and is unlikely to force a genuinely strong gallop. This shape — one unhurried front-runner controlling proceedings on Good ground over an extended trip — strongly favours horses who can race prominently or make a clean, well-timed run from midfield, as hold-up horses will find limited late acceleration on offer if the pace is modest; several redistributed hold-up types (Lakefield Flyer, Captain Connor, Makinbecon, Time Was) are unlikely to obtain their natural position at the rear and will be shuffled into midfield, compressing the field and diluting the benefit of a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gone In Sixty Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Gone In Sixty dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and kicks clear from the last flight.
scenarios.body: Gone In Sixty's natural front-running style is perfectly suited to a race with zero pace pressure, and on Good ground over 2m4½f he can conserve enough to sustain his effort to the line; his 13/15 sim-going record underlines that this surface brings out the best in him. With no hold-up horse able to generate the momentum a stronger pace would create, the prominent racers who track him closely are best placed to pounce if he tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Gone In Sixty sets a tempo that proves just fast enough to stretch the field, allowing a close tracker to overhaul him approaching the last.
scenarios.body: William Of York or a redistributed horse forced into midfield tracks the leader throughout and benefits from saving ground on the bend before producing a sustained challenge; in this scenario the winner travels prominently in second or third and needs only to be produced at the right moment. Bannister's strong sim-going record on Good and the extended trip suits a horse who can stay on powerfully from a tracking position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively honest and the hold-up horses who are shuffled into midfield find enough daylight to deliver a genuine late run.
scenarios.body: Lakefield Flyer's two wins on Good ground and a recent 1-mile win just five days ago could mean freshness tells late, with Makinbecon's course form on Good also relevant; however, both carry style-fit discounts (0.92) because they are unlikely to race in their true hold-up role. The compressed midfield means traffic risks are real and the chance of a clean passage to the outside late is reduced, limiting how likely this shape truly is.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, All Change
scenarios.trigger: If Gone In Sixty weakens sharply in the home straight as he has done in some recent finishes, scrambling the finish order.
scenarios.body: Gone In Sixty's form string includes falls and fading efforts, and if he blows up from the front after controlling affairs, a chaotic finish opens the door for any prominent or midfield horse to capitalise; Oneinthewell's hat-trick of placed efforts at similar trips and Bannister's experience at 9yo could see one grind past a spent leader. This is the lowest-probability shape because the Good ground and absence of pace pressure make a catastrophic fade less likely than on a testing surface.

watchPoints.text: Gone In Sixty's tendency to fall or fade (F and 4th in recent form) means watch whether Rian Corcoran keeps him balanced through the early hurdles — a jumping error at a key flight could unsettle the entire race shape.

Lakefield Flyer ran just five days ago; watch in the paddock and early stages for any signs of fatigue or a jockey forced wide — if Paddy Hanlon cannot find a clean route through the compressed midfield, his late run will be completely negated.

William Of York's recent record includes a pulled-up and an unseated rider — watch whether Charlie Maggs can settle him in a legitimate tracking position early, as any early resistance or jumping error from this horse will eliminate the only credible prominent challenger to Gone In Sixty.

With four natural hold-up horses all redistributed into midfield positions, the first hurdle will reveal whether the field bunches dangerously — watch for congestion on the run to the first where several horses may be fighting for the same ground in a compressed pack.

Captain Connor's inexperience on Good ground and at this distance means his conditional jockey Tom Midgley may struggle to place him effectively in a shuffled midfield — watch whether he settles and travels, or gets outpaced early and is detached before the race truly begins.

races.name: Malton Marquees Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Boom Boom Boris
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has shown form over both 17f and 20f on Good ground (2/2 in similar conditions), but his finishing runs have not converted to wins and a slow early tempo at Market Rasen is the single biggest threat to him getting competitive late.
runners_data.comment: Struggled to raise a gallop on his hurdle debut at Southwell, finishing fourth but a massive 82 lengths adrift, having shown only modest form in points. He may simply need more time to adjust to the rules game and is difficult to fancy at this stage.

runners_data.name: Brosna Town
runners_data.note: Returns from a lengthy 260-day absence (hurdles flag on record) racing prominently; modest form profile with a best of fourth, but the prominent style fits this race shape and the 3lb claim from Conor Rabbitt is a mild positive.
runners_data.comment: His flat form over middle distances suggests there's more to come once he finds his feet over hurdles, and he acts on today's going; tongue-tie applied for the first time. Yet to deliver that potential over jumps in three runs, but the underlying form is a reason to keep him in mind.

runners_data.name: Military Saint
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and going preference unknown — a significant flag in this field — but Tom Bellamy's booking for David Dennis commands respect and a finishing position of P last time out followed by a win suggests he can perform when right; watch his jumping on debut over obstacles.
runners_data.comment: A point winner, having taken a maiden pointing contest by 2.5 lengths most recently on the back of some mixed form, and he makes his rules debut here; one to note in the betting. The step from pointing to the rules game is unproven though and he sits low in our figures.

runners_data.name: Way Maker
runners_data.note: Ran just seven days ago and returns quickly, but Mickey Bowen's yard is in fine form (3/15 over 14 days) and James Bowen knows the horse; has won and placed on Good ground over 2m and 2m4f, making the trip and conditions a strong fit for a prominent display.
runners_data.comment: Heads our figures as a dual bumper winner who should be hitting his stride over hurdles; connections have a strong record in this event and he has form at this trip on a sound surface. Last run ended in an unseating but first-time cheekpieces mark a fresh angle.

runners_data.name: Rogue Impact
runners_data.note: Stepping up markedly from his maiden hurdle debut run over 2m (finished second on Good ground at Ludlow); holds a decent RPR of 120 but lacks the form depth to inspire full confidence stepping into this trip for the first time, though Jonathan Burke's booking adds interest.
runners_data.comment: Solid flat form translates well to this, and on his debut in a hurdle at Worcester he shaped promisingly — second beaten 4.5 lengths despite expending too much energy early on. First-time cheekpieces here should help him settle and he's capable of going one better.

runners_data.name: Lipstick Traces
runners_data.note: Has consistent form figures of 3-5 across varied trips and conditions — a solid performer — but her natural inclination is to race further back than the pace map shows, and in a small field where the pace is expected to be modest, getting a meaningful late run from off the bridle is structurally difficult here.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without threatening in recent starts — her last outing at Cartmel saw her beaten nine lengths but the form was in line with her level — and she handles today's distance and ground well. she's yet to find the improvement her current mark asks for, which is the sticking point.

runners_data.name: Little Lady Rock
runners_data.note: Market Rasen's lone front runner whose record shows four consecutive placed efforts on Good ground and who will enjoy a completely uncontested lead; the STYLE_FIT tag notes she is slightly out of role in this map but in reality she is the one horse guaranteed her preferred position, which is a tangible advantage.
runners_data.comment: Her bumper form showed plenty of consistency and she acts on today's going; the hurdling debut at Worcester was rough — she raced green and was well beaten — but there's every reason to expect improvement now she's had that experience. She rates one of the leading threats if her jumping clicks.

races.paceDynamic: Little Lady Rock is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should stride out from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m4½f at Market Rasen. Way Maker and Brosna Town are the prominent types who will track her closely, meaning the race is likely to develop into a steady-paced procession through the first half before tempo builds turning in. The field holds more hold-up types than can naturally settle at the rear — Lipstick Traces is a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield, meaning she is unlikely to find her natural position and her late-running chance is structurally compromised. This race shape — a single unhurried pace-setter, modest early tempo, and a small field of seven — overwhelmingly favours horses that can travel prominently in the slipstream of Little Lady Rock and produce their effort from the home turn, rewarding the prominent-to-lead profile most cleanly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled lead, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If Little Lady Rock sets an uncontested, moderate gallop and the race is decided by those sitting second or third throughout.
scenarios.body: Little Lady Rock dictates from the front on her own terms with Way Maker and Brosna Town tracking without pressure, and the winner emerges from this small prominent group as the pace lifts from the third-last hurdle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader gallops rivals flat
scenarios.trigger: If Little Lady Rock sets a stronger-than-expected pace that strings the field out and grinds down hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A genuine front-running tempo over 2m4½f on Good ground would suit a horse with proven staying stamina at the head of affairs, leaving hold-up types with too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse swoops late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the prominent horses tie up inside the final two flights and a closer runs past.
scenarios.body: Boom Boom Boris, who has run well in similar Good-ground conditions, would be the most likely beneficiary if those at the front give a true target, though the early pace must be honest for this to materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical chaos, race collapses
scenarios.trigger: If there is interference, a fall or major jumping error that reshapes the race entirely from an early stage.
scenarios.body: A seven-runner maiden hurdle with lightly raced types including Military Saint (lightly raced, going unknown) carries some risk of a race-altering incident, opening the door to an unexpected outcome.

watchPoints.text: Little Lady Rock's jumping must be monitored from the off — if she makes a significant error at an early flight, the entire race shape collapses and hold-up horses gain a structural advantage they would not otherwise have.

Military Saint's going preference is flagged unknown and he is lightly raced over hurdles; if he jumps poorly or jumps to his right on the right-handed Market Rasen circuit, he could impede those tracking the leader, particularly Way Maker.

Way Maker runs just seven days after his last start — watch his paddock demeanour and early race behaviour for any sign of fatigue or freshness that could cause him to over-race behind the leader and compromise his chance.

Lipstick Traces, a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield, will need to find a clear run turning for home in a compact seven-runner field; watch for her being trapped on the inner if Little Lady Rock slows the pace and the field compresses before the second-last.

Brosna Town returns from 260 days off and, while the prominent style suits this race shape, monitor his jumping fluency early — a rusty jumper returning from a long absence over hurdles can lose crucial lengths at the first flight that are hard to recover in a small field.

races.name: ECIS Say Yes To Solar Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Fidendum
runners_data.note: Most likely to be the genuine closer in this race; has winning and placed form at this trip on Good ground, wears headgear, and Nick Slatter's 3lb claim helps offset the weight; 38 days since last run is manageable but the hold-up style depends on Granny Hawkins setting enough of a tempo to create a gap.
runners_data.comment: Went close at Worcester last time, beaten a length despite doing too much early on his first handicap start, which tells you his ability is there; handles 2m on a sound surface. Hood and tongue-tie on for the first time here, which should help him produce his best.

runners_data.name: Granny Hawkins
runners_data.note: Alan King's in-form stable (1/12 last 14 days) sends the race's key pace-setter here with three wins from three starts at 16f on Good — she owns this shape, though a 77-day absence and a STYLE_FIT flag (she is racing in her natural role but the tag reflects marginal field concern) are worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last five, including a two-and-a-half-length handicap success at Stratford last time despite encountering trouble in running — the record speaks and she handles this trip and going well. The trainer is in good form, there's a short layoff to overcome, but she rates the likeliest winner.

runners_data.name: Tilehurst
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes over on this consistent five-year-old who has finished placed in four of his last five on Good ground; operating prominently suits him perfectly in this race shape, and a 92-day break is the only question mark against his obvious tactical suitability.
runners_data.comment: A consistent placer prior to his Huntingdon flop — beaten 30 lengths there with nothing to mitigate it — and he handles the trip and conditions well enough. A fresh run from a short layoff, but he needs to bounce back from that effort to be competitive here.

runners_data.name: Kaikoura
runners_data.note: The significant lay-off of 267 days since her last run is the headline concern, and her form figures in larger fields at distance (a 10th and a 7th) suggest she struggles when the race is not run to suit; Nathan Moscrop partners her for Susan Corbett's yard, which has one winner from five runners in the last fortnight.
runners_data.comment: His Irish form suggests the mark is workable over this sort of trip, but nine months off the track is a significant question mark; a first run for a new stable adds further uncertainty. He may simply need this to find his footing and is hard to fancy strongly in that context.

runners_data.name: Diesel Line
runners_data.note: James Bowen rides this veteran prominently-styled eight-year-old who wears a tongue strap; his Good-ground form shows consistent placing (multiple thirds and fourths at this trip) but he has not won for some time, and a fall last time (form: 3344-F) is a jumping confidence question worth watching.
runners_data.comment: His latest outing ended in a fall at Uttoxeter, which doesn't reflect his ability — he'd been posting consistent placed finishes prior and handles 2m on a sound surface. Tongue-tie applied for the first time here and a break since; the fall is expected to leave no mark and he's entitled to come on.

runners_data.name: Crown Of India
runners_data.note: Returned quickly (18 days) for Alex Hales, who has one winner from two runners in the last fortnight; the horse's truest inclination is to race off the pace and finish late, but with multiple hold-up types in this field he will likely find himself running in midfield rather than from the rear, which is not his optimal vehicle for a winning run.
runners_data.comment: Back to something like his best form, with a narrow three-quarter-length win at Worcester two runs back followed by a solid second last time, beaten five lengths off 93; 1lb higher now but handles this distance on good ground well. An inconsistent sort overall, but the recent upturn makes him a genuine contender.

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's nine-year-old ran just 12 days ago and was placed last time (a third); this horse is a genuine hold-up performer by inclination, sitting closer to midfield in the race map than his natural style demands because the field is congested at the rear — his 0W3P record on similar going and 15 runs on Good without a win are sobering data points.
runners_data.comment: Third beaten 3.5 lengths at Newton Abbot last time on this exact mark — a fair effort after a break, and he handles the distance well — but he has a tendency to over-race and his reliability is questionable; this form needs building on before he can be trusted.

races.paceDynamic: Granny Hawkins is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no credible challenger willing to dispute the lead, she should slide into an uncontested role and dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good ground over 2m½f. Tilehurst and Diesel Line carry prominent styles and will look to track close behind, creating a compact early formation rather than a strung-out, searching tempo. The race shape is therefore likely to be a steadily-run lead that quickens in the back straight and asks questions at the final flights — a profile that rewards horses travelling fluently within themselves and attacking late, but not so late that they have nothing to pick up. That verdict favours hold-up horses who can close through a race that does not fall apart early, but the critical caveat is that Crown Of India and Applejack Poet — both true hold-up types — have been pushed into the midfield mapping because the field holds more rear-of-field operators than the pace shape can accommodate at the back; Granny Hawkins and Tilehurst are most likely to secure the natural prominent positions, meaning the truest closers may not get the separation they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Granny Hawkins Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Granny Hawkins leads unchallenged, sets a controlled pace and finds enough in the tank to repel late challengers at the last.
scenarios.body: She dictates every yard, conserving energy through the flat, and her superior recent form (three wins in four on Good ground) suggests she can sustain the effort to the line; a steady tempo means the lead is not given up easily.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Sweep Past Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Tilehurst or Diesel Line press Granny Hawkins harder than expected and the leader fades approaching the last.
scenarios.body: A fractionally stronger pace drains the leader in the final half-mile, allowing a prominent tracker who has conserved energy just off the pace to sweep past and hold on; Tilehurst's consistent placing record and Sean Bowen's tactical acumen suit this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a true closer can reel in the principals in the final flight.
scenarios.body: Fidendum has the most credible hold-up profile in this field with genuine winning form on Good ground at this trip, and a strong final-flight finish could peg back a tiring leader; however, the compressed pace makes a truly strung-out race unlikely, limiting how much ground closers can make.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Finish, All Bets Off
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, interference or an unusually strong breakaway pace scrambles the expected order.
scenarios.body: In a small field of seven, a single faller or a badly-timed blunder at a critical flight could promote an unconsidered runner; Kaikoura has the class ceiling and course form to profit from chaos, though her 267-day absence is a significant concern against fresher rivals.

watchPoints.text: Granny Hawkins jumping — she sets the race shape entirely, so any blunder at a flight would immediately disrupt the pace map and open the race for Tilehurst or Diesel Line to inherit the lead.

Diesel Line's last run ended in a fall; watch his jumping closely in the early stages, as a repeat incident in a field of only seven would have a significant effect on the race shape and could bring down other prominent runners.

Kaikoura's 267-day absence means she may not be tuned to race fitness; if she travels poorly early or is gently handled, she effectively reduces the field to six and removes any outside-pace threat from the rear.

Crown Of India and Applejack Poet are both true hold-up horses likely to race closer than ideal — if both get shuffled forward against their nature in the early stages, the midfield could become congested and interfere with Fidendum's intended hold-up run.

The Good ground is confirmed consistent across all Market Rasen races today, so no late-changing surface to alter expectations — pace should hold, and the early leader's energy will not be sapped by unexpectedly testing conditions.

races.name: Stay At The Market Rasen Racecourse Caravan Park Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Beny Nahar Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up stayer with 2 wins and 7 places from 15 similar-going runs; Henry Hogarth yard in quiet form (0/0 T14) but horse is race-fit at 22 days and the 2m7f trip suits based on hist distances; tongue-tie noted.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Hexham last time after apparently hitting a flat spot when asked to quicken — stamina over today's extended trip may be an issue. Consistent on a sound surface, he acts here and a first-time tongue-tie could sharpen him; ranked 4th on our figures.

runners_data.name: I Am Spider Man
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up specialist with four consecutive top-3 finishes including two seconds over 2m6f on Good; Barry John Murphy yard is 0/9 in 14 days which tempers confidence, but the form profile and trip are excellent.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 3 lengths at Newton Abbot last time, going well until being worn down in the closing stages, I Am Spider Man has placed in each of his last four starts. Top-rated on our figures, he acts over this distance on good ground and looks capable of going one better.

runners_data.name: Lunar Morning
runners_data.note: Marked as the race's lone front-runner, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) signals this is out of character; visor on, 5-year-old for Max Comley with limited Good-ground experience (2/3 sim-going) — its ability to control from the front shapes the entire race but its own winning chance is moderated by the role misfit.
runners_data.comment: Showed better form when stepped up in trip last time here, finishing 9 lengths third in a maiden hurdle while wearing a visor for the first time — that headgear is retained today. Acts on this ground at today's trip and looks the type to progress once handicapping; ranked 5th.

runners_data.name: Indian Sunbird
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a remarkable 15/15 similar-going record and three wins among those; Harry Bannister partners a mare who won over 2m5f on Good and finished second here over 2m4f — conditions are squarely in her favour and the trip is well within range.
runners_data.comment: Back to something like his best at Southwell last time, beaten 3¼l on a slightly lower mark, Indian Sunbird usually settles in the rear and is effective at today's trip and going. Ranked 7th on our figures, his mark looks about right and he can be competitive.

runners_data.name: Jack The Savage
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 2m6f on Good, his second win at that distance; hold-up style suits the scenario here, 13 of 15 similar-going runs have produced a finish, and the tongue-plus headgear combination (tp) is retained — Sean Bowen booking adds confidence.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Fontwell last time off a 5lb lower mark, making full use of a clear lead and holding on by a neck. Acts over today's trip on sound ground; first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces, and looks fairly handicapped on his best despite the rise in mark.

runners_data.name: Copper Beach
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with five places from 10 similar-going runs but no win in that sample; Oscar Palmer takes a 7lb claim, which helps with the 9-year-old's OR of 94, but consistent placing without winning is a recurring theme.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 9½l at Southwell last time but that followed three close seconds that show he retains his ability — on his old form he holds a major advantage over these rivals. Effective here and over this distance on sound ground; first-time tongue-tie, and rated 2nd on our figures.

runners_data.name: Larkfield Lusive
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 2m4f on Good and has three Good-ground wins from 10 similar outings; Brian Hughes in the saddle for LJ Morgan yard, prominent style suits this race shape, and the headgear (p) is retained — the step up to 2m7f is the only query.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Southwell last time off a 4lb lower mark, showing a willing attitude over a longer trip, and has been in good heart since that success. First-time cheekpieces; acts on this ground and distance, but our figures rate him 9th and the mark has stiffened.

runners_data.name: You Did
runners_data.note: Has been off 150 days and all five hist runs were on Soft ground (sim-going only 1/1 on Good from 4 runs); Brian Ellison yard in strong form (2/24 T14) but the layoff, going switch and soft-ground form record make this a significant risk at 2m7f.
runners_data.comment: Off for 150 days after a pull-up at Doncaster on his last outing, You Did had shown good form prior — landing two races in his last five. Acts here over today's trip; first-time cheekpieces, though he needs to find more off his current mark to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Matoury
runners_data.note: Won last time at 16 days ago over 2m3f on Good; William Maggs claims 3lb, hold-up style with tongue-tie, and the two wins from 11 similar-going runs came at shorter — the step to 2m7f is a genuine query but recent form is live.
runners_data.comment: Edged out the runner-up by a short head in a handicap here last time off a 6lb lower mark, Matoury goes well at this track and the trip suits. Inconsistent overall, but his affinity for Market Rasen makes him of interest despite being rated 11th; first-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Star Vantage
runners_data.note: Has run four consecutive fourths including over 2m7f on Good; natural hold-up type whose genuine racing style has been pushed into a mid-division mapping by the congested rear — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) reflects the compromise, and a winless sim-going record (0/9 with 2 places) limits enthusiasm regardless of scenario.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with encouragement when fourth at Hexham last time, beaten 6 lengths, and remains on a workable mark despite a succession of fourths in recent starts. Stays well, acts here on this going; first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces, and consistently competitive — the maiden tag is the one nagging concern.

runners_data.name: The Roc Hopper
runners_data.note: Ran second last time over 2m2f on Good for the Rebecca Menzies yard; a true hold-up horse that the race shape has compressed into mid-division, and the sim-going record is thin (0/9 one place) — Nathan Moscrop rides and the horse needs a clear run that the congested field may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Beaten less than a length at Cartmel last time off a 3lb lower mark, unable to hold off a racefitter rival, The Roc Hopper can improve on that encouraging effort. Acts at today's distance on this ground; first-time hood and tongue-tie, but trainer badly out of form and rated 10th.

runners_data.name: Ramaah
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for Sarah-Jayne Davies whose four sim-going runs on Good have produced no win and two places; genuine hold-up racer placed into mid-division by the crowded rear, visor fitted, and the form over shorter trips (1m8f–1m11f in hist) makes 2m7f a stamina question as much as a tactical one.
runners_data.comment: Found the early pace beyond him but stayed on well to take third here last time, shaped as a progressive stayer with room to improve. First-time visor; ranked last on our figures and his best form has come on softer ground, but the trip should suit.

races.paceDynamic: Lunar Morning is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner field over 2m7f on Good ground, and with no natural rival to push the pace, Tom Broughton (claiming 3lb) can dictate a controlled, metronomic gallop that suits a horse already noted as racing out of its natural role — meaning the pace is real but not truly pressured. Behind, Indian Sunbird, Copper Beach, Larkfield Lusive and You Did all want to race prominently, creating genuine competition for the chasing positions and ensuring the race is not falsely run, but Lunar Morning should still clear away to control the tempo from the front. The hold-up contingent — Beny Nahar Road, I Am Spider Man, Jack The Savage and Matoury — are true closers who will need the pace to be genuine enough over this staying trip to allow them to deliver their runs, and on Good ground over 2m7f with one clear pace-setter, the gallop should be honest enough to reward that profile. This race shape most strongly favours confirmed hold-up and off-the-pace stayers who can travel within themselves before mounting sustained challenges from three out, with the steady but uncontested front pace providing the ideal tempo for closers to land late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Lunar Morning bowls clear and the prominent pack settles into a rhythm behind without disrupting the steady pace.
scenarios.body: Lunar Morning sets a sustainable gallop uncontested and the prominent horses burn energy competing amongst themselves for the chasing slots, leaving the true closers with a genuine target to pick off in the straight; patient hold-up horses who travel well on Good ground over the full 2m7f are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of prominent types — Indian Sunbird, Copper Beach, Larkfield Lusive — press forward and turn this into a more searching test from halfway.
scenarios.body: A more competitive early gallop suits the prominent horses who can sit just off the pace in a handy position and grind out the staying trip, with Indian Sunbird's excellent Going record (15/15 sim-going) and Larkfield Lusive's recent win giving them strong claims.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and the field spreads wide, allowing true hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: With a single uncontested pace-setter on Good ground, there is a risk the early gallop is too steady and the race turns into a sprint finish; hold-up horses with high form figures at the trip on similar ground are best placed if that closing burst is decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded prominent group causes interference or a faller disrupts the pace shape entirely, forcing a messy outcome.
scenarios.body: Star Vantage, The Roc Hopper and Ramaah are all true hold-up horses compressed into mid-division by the race shape and may find themselves with nowhere to go in traffic; if a chaotic scenario opens gaps unexpectedly, one of these could benefit from a clearer route than expected.

watchPoints.text: Lunar Morning's ability to control the pace unchallenged is the single biggest race-shape lever — if Indian Sunbird or Larkfield Lusive push forward to pressure the front, the entire dynamic shifts from a controlled solo lead to a grinding test.

You Did has been off 150 days, all meaningful form is on Soft ground, and the jump to 2m7f on Good is a treble question mark — monitor market moves but form evidence is very thin for this surface and distance.

The Roc Hopper, Star Vantage and Ramaah are all natural hold-up horses packed into mid-division by the race shape; watch for traffic problems on the final bend as all three may be seeking the same gap at the same time.

Jack The Savage is the only hold-up horse in the field carrying a winning run at this exact distance (2m6f) on Good ground into the race — Sean Bowen's awareness of that profile makes him one to track from three out.

Indian Sunbird's 15/15 similar-going record is the standout stats flag in this field — if the pace scenario allows her to be prominent without burning petrol, she becomes a benchmark for others to beat in the straight.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Fringill Dike
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Jedd O'Keeffe, whose stable is currently cold (0/3 in 14 days), but Fringill Dike himself finished 1st last time out 23 days ago over a similar trip on good ground, giving it strong recent form claims; blinkers worn and 13 of 15 similar-going runs suggest the conditions are right.
runners_data.comment: Dropped in class and down 7lb in the weights, he dominated a handicap here last time by 9 lengths, confirming he sees out this trip on decent ground. First-time blinkers, but he's well treated on his better form and rates a clear danger.

runners_data.name: Authorised Speed
runners_data.note: Returning after a massive 785-day absence for Gary & Josh Moore, whose stable is in reasonable nick (4/21 T14), but that layoff is a dominant concern; the STYLE_FIT flag signals it may not fully command the front-running role as expected, and its record on good ground is thin (2/15 similar-going runs, 0W0P), making it a significant risk at the head of affairs.
runners_data.comment: Tops our figures despite a layoff of more than two years, and holds form over this sort of trip; he's the one to beat if fit and forward. Ground with some give suits him best, and today's conditions may not be entirely ideal, though he remains a genuine threat on the strength of older form.

runners_data.name: Regal Renaissance
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes over on a horse in superb current form — back-to-back wins (form: F42-11), including two victories over today's trip on good ground; Jack Jones's yard is quiet (0/9 T14) but Regal Renaissance's own profile is compelling, and its prominent style means it will be ideally placed to challenge Authorised Speed whenever that horse's stamina gives way.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back handicap successes make her hard to dismiss — including a nine-length display last time off a mark 5lb below today's — and she handles this trip and conditions well. Up only 3lb for that effort, consistent and progressive, she can extend her sequence here.

runners_data.name: Gateau De Miel
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer wearing a tongue-tie, trained by Fergal O'Brien who has had 2 winners from 10 in 14 days; lightly freshed up at 16 days since last run and won over a similar trip on good ground last time out, but at OR 114 in a 4-runner field it faces a stiff task, and its age (10) adds a small jumping-reliability caveat over fences.
runners_data.comment: Showed his potential when landing a handicap by 10 lengths at Stratford two runs back, though he was well off that level in a higher grade last time, beaten a long way. Tongue-tie applied and 1lb lower here, his connections have a strong record in this event; consistency is the main doubt.

races.paceDynamic: Authorised Speed is the lone confirmed front-runner in a small field of four, and with no other horse likely to dispute the lead, Caoilin Quinn's mount will dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from the outset over 2m5½f on good ground at Market Rasen. Regal Renaissance is the other prominent type and will sit closest in behind, likely tracking Authorised Speed through the early stages, while Fringill Dike and Gateau De Miel will settle in rear as natural hold-up performers. The key caveat is that Authorised Speed returns from 785 days off the track and carries a STYLE_FIT discount, meaning the pace it sets may be modest and potentially vulnerable to error or fade in the closing stages rather than a dominant front-running display. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent closers who can travel within themselves and produce a sustained finishing effort from the final fence — Regal Renaissance's front-running form and Fringill Dike's closing profile from the rear are the two styles best positioned to exploit a potentially limited pace-setter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Swamped
scenarios.trigger: If Authorised Speed sets a moderate uncontested gallop but fades inside the final two fences after its long absence.
scenarios.body: Regal Renaissance tracks the leader throughout and produces the most fluid jump at the last to assert, benefiting from a prominent position without ever having to do hard work; closers arrive late but the proximity of Regal Renaissance proves decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow, compressing the race into a sprint finish that rewards the freshest pair of legs from the rear.
scenarios.body: Fringill Dike and Gateau De Miel arrive with momentum from off the pace and swamp those who have done more work earlier; Fringill Dike's course-applicable good-ground form and Sean Quinlan's tactical awareness make it the most likely beneficiary of a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Authorised Speed Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If Authorised Speed, despite its 785-day absence, jumps boldly and sustains a strong enough gallop to deny the chasers.
scenarios.body: The long layoff and STYLE_FIT flag make this outcome unlikely, but if the horse has been produced cherry-ripe by Gary & Josh Moore and jumps cleanly throughout, it could hold on up the run-in; its form in similar going is limited to just 2/15 runs, further reducing confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Reduces Field
scenarios.trigger: If a faller or unseated rider disrupts the shape mid-race, forcing survivors to adjust tactics entirely.
scenarios.body: With only four runners any incident dramatically alters the dynamic, potentially gifting a surviving front-runner a walkover finish or exposing a hold-up horse that cannot quicken when asked from further back than planned; Gateau De Miel's tongue-tie and 10-year age profile add a minor jumping-safety concern.

watchPoints.text: Authorised Speed's jumping — 785 days off the track means its fence-jumping sharpness is entirely unknown; a bad error early could end the race or dramatically compromise the pace it sets.

Regal Renaissance's proximity to the leader — Sean Bowen will want to sit tight on Authorised Speed's quarters, but if the pace is very slow he risks getting outsprinted by fresher hold-up horses arriving late from Fringill Dike or Gateau De Miel.

Fringill Dike's finishing effort — it won last time but Jedd O'Keeffe's stable is 0/3 in the last 14 days, and if the pace is genuinely slow the hold-up horse may not get the gaps it needs in a small field to produce its best.

Gateau De Miel tongue-tie effect — the headgear is noted and worth watching at the start; if it travels comfortably mid-race with Broughton conserving its energy, it could improve its position more significantly than its OR 114 suggests in a race this small.

races.name: Wild West Beer Fest Saturday 26th September Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Ballydisco
runners_data.note: Strong headgear flag (tongue-tie/pads), Tom Lacey yard in modest 14-day form, but this 9yo has five runs on Good or similar and handles the trip — a genuine hold-up operator who needs things to happen in front of him in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Finished second on his seasonal reappearance at Uttoxeter, running to his level after a layoff, and stays further than today's trip on any ground. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces here; he tops our figures but yet to win over fences remains the note of caution.

runners_data.name: Zestful Hope
runners_data.note: James Bowen takes the ride for Longsdon whose yard is 0/4 in the last 14 days, and Zestful Hope's last win came on Good ground; placed third at 19f on soft recently suggests 24f-plus suits, but prominent-type tendencies noted in headgear history.
runners_data.comment: His Warwick run last time was more of a blowout — fourth beaten 38 lengths — and he's inconsistent, but he handles this distance and going well and first-time cheekpieces add a new variable. A fresher look could revive him, though confidence in his reliability is limited.

runners_data.name: Ribeye
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who will set the tempo from flag to finish; 11 years old, pulled up twice recently, and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 signals he is carrying more weight than suits, but if he travels comfortably in front his experience dictates the race shape entirely.
runners_data.comment: Has a strong record in this event — successful here last year — but the form since has been poor, pulling up twice in recent starts. He acts on today's ground and is held up, but needs to drop in grade to compete here and rates an unlikely winner at present.

runners_data.name: Queens Wish
runners_data.note: Seven placed runs from 11 starts on similar going is a standout stat — this 7yo is the most consistent horse in the field on Good ground, Robert Dunne retains, and she ran well over 24f at Goodwood last time; genuine hold-up profile suits the expected shape.
runners_data.comment: A consistent performer who handles this distance and going, she was runner-up at Uttoxeter last time, beaten nine lengths while making the running on an easy lead. That form is about her level but she sits low in our figures and looks an unlikely winner in this company.

runners_data.name: Galway Reel
runners_data.note: Ian Williams has an excellent 5/34 strike rate in the 14-day window and Sean Bowen is a major booking; his ground stats (14/15 on Good) are exceptional, though he is a natural hold-up horse whose best position may be harder to secure here given the field composition.
runners_data.comment: A course-and-distance winner over hurdles and fences on a fair mark, but his last outing at Uttoxeter was one where he was arguably asked to reappear too quickly. First-time cheekpieces now with conditions to suit, he's capable of running a big race back at a venue where he's proven himself.

runners_data.name: Just A Memory
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien sends him out with a 2/10 14-day record, and his two placings have come on Good and Soft ground at 24-26f; he finished second last time out, but his true rear-of-field style means he needs a truly run race to deliver — the mapped midfield position overstates his likely early pitch.
runners_data.comment: Her chase mark is fair enough but reliability is the question — her latest Newton Abbot run saw her pushed forward too hard, finishing a remote third by 43 lengths. Acts on this going and should get the trip, but being overworked in front could recur.

runners_data.name: Friends Don't Ask
runners_data.note: 11yo with every one of her last five runs placing at 2nd, 3rd, or 4th — a model of consistency but without a win; a natural hold-up horse filling midfield on the map due to field composition, and her form figures on Good ground (2-4-2-3-3) are remarkably solid for Charlie Maggs (3lb claimer) and a small yard.
runners_data.comment: Back to his best last time at Bangor-on-Dee, runner-up beaten 2.25 lengths off this exact mark — he races off the front foot and handles 3m on good ground well. Quick turnaround from nine days ago but first-time cheekpieces add a new dimension; inconsistency is the caveat but the recent form is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Huckleberry Sting
runners_data.note: Progressing 7yo — won at 24f on Good ground two runs ago and placed twice since; headgear (tongue-tie) is retained and Jack Andrews is a solid booking; sits comfortably second on the map and his recent upward trajectory makes him interesting if the pace is sustainable.
runners_data.comment: Held up in his races, he landed a five-length success at Bangor-on-Dee three starts back off a mark 10lb lower, and ran with credit last time — third beaten four lengths — on the same mark as today. First-time tongue-tie here; consistent enough in form but the handicapper may have caught up with him.

runners_data.name: On The Platform
runners_data.note: Won on Soft ground and has a placed run on Good, but that winning run came 50 days ago and his form figures either side of it include a pull-up and a fifth; prominent style suits the race shape but his record for the Belinda Clarke yard at 0W5P on similar ground is a caution.
runners_data.comment: Tired late at Bangor-on-Dee last time after a break, finishing fifth beaten 8.25 lengths but running to his level; handles this distance on a sound surface. First-time cheekpieces and a short layoff since — inconsistent but should come on from that run.

races.paceDynamic: Ribeye is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 3m handicap chase and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a sustainable, controlled gallop from the outset — this is not a race that will be run at a frenetic pace. Huckleberry Sting and On The Platform are the only other prominent-style runners and will likely sit just behind Ribeye, creating a small lead group ahead of a larger chasing pack. The hold-up contingent — Ballydisco, Zestful Hope, and Queens Wish — will have genuine cover and room to manoeuvre from the rear, while Galway Reel, Just A Memory, and Friends Don't Ask are true hold-up horses redistributed toward midfield on the map because there are more rear-of-field types than the race shape can accommodate at the back. The field holds more hold-up types than can all get their natural position; of those redistributed, Galway Reel (Sean Bowen, strong Good-ground profile) and Just A Memory are most likely to secure a forward pitch than their tag suggests. A steady-run, sustainable pace over 3m on Good ground at Market Rasen will favour horses with genuine class and stamina who can travel smoothly through the race and pick up in the home straight — prominent runners who settle well and hold-up types with strong Good-ground form are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ribeye Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ribeye dictates a fair but uncontested gallop and the race develops into a test of jumping fluency and sustained gallop.
scenarios.body: Ribeye leads at a pace that suits those travelling within themselves just behind, and Huckleberry Sting or On The Platform — who have the natural gate speed to sit close — are handed a box-seat position without burning reserves. With no pace injection from rivals, the front rank arrives at the last with enough left to hold on as hold-up horses fail to find the required late burst on Good ground over this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ribeye's gallop is just honest enough to set up a proper finish and the genuine hold-up runners pick their way through in the straight.
scenarios.body: Ballydisco, Zestful Hope, or Queens Wish track the pace at a comfortable distance and produce a staying run from the final fence as the front rank begins to tire. Good ground and 3m suit patient hold-up horses who have the stamina profile, and Queens Wish's consistent placed record on Good ground makes her particularly interesting in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Galway Reel Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Sean Bowen pushes Galway Reel forward from his redistributed midfield position to secure a genuinely prominent pitch early.
scenarios.body: Galway Reel's dominant Good-ground form (14 of 15 runs on similar ground) and Ian Williams' strong 14-day record give him every chance if he can get close enough to land a blow in the straight. The STYLE_FIT discount is real — he is a natural hold-up horse asked to race forward — but Bowen's tactical intelligence means this scenario cannot be dismissed entirely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Carnage From Jumping Errors
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses through fences being hit and the race dissolves into an untidy, stop-start affair.
scenarios.body: At 3m over fences, with an 11-year-old Ribeye leading and older handicappers throughout the field, a jumping incident at a key fence could scatter the race order and benefit whoever avoids trouble. Friends Don't Ask's consistent place-form on all types of Good ground and experience over the trip makes her a potential beneficiary of a messy race.

watchPoints.text: Ribeye's jumping — if he makes a significant error at any of the early fences his role as pace-setter collapses immediately and the entire race shape is redrawn.

Galway Reel's early positioning — watch whether Sean Bowen elects to push forward or settles back; if Galway Reel secures a prominent pitch rather than his natural hold-up position it transforms his winning chance.

Friends Don't Ask's weight at 149lbs for an 11yo — the lowest-weighted runner in the field gets a significant advantage on handicap terms but needs the race to be genuinely run to deliver her consistent late effort.
Queens Wish's jumping — she has placed in four of her last five over Good ground but has yet to win over fences; a clean round at 3m will be essential to converting her consistency into a result.

Huckleberry Sting's stamina — all three of his placed recent runs have been at 24f; this step up to 3m (24f equivalent is his ceiling so far) is the key unknown, and how he travels jumping the last few fences will reveal whether the trip is stretching him.

races.name: Boxing Day At The Races On Sale Now! Open Maiden NH Flat Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Don De La Frontera
runners_data.comment: Beaten out of sight in his latest point outing and making little impression in points overall, Don De La Frontera is hard to recommend ranked last on our figures. The stable has produced bumper debut winners this year — market support would be the trigger to reconsider.

runners_data.name: Ifyouhaveaplan
runners_data.comment: Showed much better form when runner-up at Tabley latest, beaten 3 lengths in a maiden point, and returns after a short break. Placed in a point race, he may still be learning the Rules game, but has enough about him to be considered at 5th on our figures.

runners_data.name: Litaque
runners_data.comment: Made a pleasing debut at Worcester, 8¼l third in a bumper, and has winning form in points. The stable has a strong record in this race, and rated 2nd on our figures, Litaque is a serious contender — the modest nature of the point win is his only reservation.

runners_data.name: Masterius
runners_data.comment: Narrowly denied on his debut at this course and trip, beaten just a head in a bumper here 16 days ago, Masterius is the form pick with scope to build further. Rated 1st on our figures, he acts on this going and looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Parisian Fair
runners_data.comment: A debut run from a stable capable of landing bumpers first time out, Parisian Fair is a Way To Paris gelding out of a dam who stayed at 14 furlongs. His market moves on the day are worth following.

runners_data.name: Secret Message
runners_data.comment: A Flat-bred Ghaiyyath gelding making his debut, Secret Message has a half-brother who landed a Listed prize and a dam who showed smart ability on the level. Stamina questions remain, though betting interest on the day would make him more compelling.

runners_data.name: Ayla's Star
runners_data.comment: A Yorgunnabelucky mare making her debut in a first-time tongue-tie, Ayla's Star is bred from staying bloodlines — her dam showed moderate form from 10 to 19 furlongs. This initial run looks likely to be a learning experience, though the pedigree has staying potential for the future.

runners_data.name: Guerdale
runners_data.comment: Unable to match the early gallop on her bumper debut at Southwell, Guerdale was well beaten and has plenty to find against more exposed rivals here. With just the one run behind her, she needs significant improvement to feature.

runners_data.name: Parish Girl
runners_data.comment: Showed plenty on her bumper debut at Plumpton, finishing third with the form subsequently validated by later events. Acts on this going and suits today's trip; rated 4th on our figures, she looks set to build on that experience and is a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Poppieholla
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on her only start — an Amateurs' bumper at Worcester where she couldn't match the early pace — Poppieholla arrives with little form to assess but was well fancied on debut, suggesting connections expect better. A step up on that initial effort is expected.

runners_data.name: Zandahar
runners_data.comment: Finished runner-up on her bumper debut at Plumpton, beaten 5½l, with subsequent events backing up that debut form. Acts on this going at today's trip and should progress; rated 3rd on our figures, she is one of the stronger dangers in this field.
